mountains.name: Kuwohi
mountains.inspirational_story: The restoration of its Cherokee name transforms this towering peak from a tourist stop into a living monument of peace and enduring Indigenous heritage.
mountains.fun_fact: It stands proudly as the highest point along the entire 2,192-mile Appalachian Trail.

mountains.name: Mount Blue Sky
mountains.inspirational_story: Its high-altitude alpine gardens host bristlecone pines that have thrived on adversity for 1,700 years, silently enduring extreme winds.
mountains.fun_fact: It boasts the highest continuous paved road in North America, terminating near 14,264 feet.

mountains.name: Pikes Peak
mountains.inspirational_story: Peter Strudwick, born without feet and with missing hands, completed the grueling ascent and marathon in 1972, proving the limitless power of human will.
mountains.fun_fact: The spectacular view from its summit inspired Katherine Lee Bates to write the lyrics to 'America the Beautiful'.

mountains.name: Haleakala
mountains.inspirational_story: Watching the sunrise above a 'waterfall of fog' offers visitors a primordial, comforting solitude that feels like witnessing the birth of a star.
mountains.fun_fact: Despite being so close to the equator, temperatures at the summit can rapidly plummet to near-freezing.

mountains.name: Mauna Kea
mountains.inspirational_story: Rising dramatically from the deep ocean floor, it offers a serene, cloud-piercing vantage point where humanity peers into the deepest reaches of the cosmos.
mountains.fun_fact: When measured from its base on the ocean floor to its summit, it is significantly taller than Mount Everest.

mountains.name: Mount Washington
mountains.inspirational_story: Volunteers like Sandy and Joan Kurtz have dedicated nearly 50 years to supporting the mountain's observatory, fostering a deep community of perseverance.
mountains.fun_fact: Early Native Americans called it 'Agiocochook' and considered it the sacred home of the gods.

mountains.name: Mount Mitchell
mountains.inspirational_story: Elisha Mitchell dedicated his life to surveying its heights and ultimately lost his life on its slopes, but his devotion led to the creation of North Carolina's first state park.
mountains.fun_fact: It stands as the highest peak in North America east of the Mississippi River.

mountains.name: Cadillac Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: The Wabanaki, 'People of the Dawn Land,' have revered this place for generations, finding coastal serenity in the breaking of the first light.
mountains.fun_fact: During the winter, it is the first place in the United States to witness the sunrise.

mountains.name: Sassafras Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: The mountain's summit, formed by deep geological time and continental collisions, now offers a peaceful, wheelchair-accessible sanctuary to enjoy the majesty of nature.
mountains.fun_fact: It serves as the separation point for three distinct watersheds, sending water to both the Atlantic and the Gulf.

mountains.name: Brasstown Bald
mountains.inspirational_story: Rising above the surrounding valleys, its name comes from the Cherokee 'Itse'yi,' meaning 'a place of fresh green,' symbolizing renewal and life.
mountains.fun_fact: The observation deck provides a clear view of four different states simultaneously.

mountains.name: Cheaha Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Amidst the struggles of the Great Depression, the Civilian Conservation Corps worked tirelessly to replant its forests and build peaceful trails for future generations.
mountains.fun_fact: It is one of only five state high points that still retains its original Indigenous name, derived from the Creek word for 'high place'.

mountains.name: Mount Magazine
mountains.inspirational_story: Its isolated, flat-topped plateau became a safe haven and refuge for those seeking solace and cool breezes above the harsh valley temperatures.
mountains.fun_fact: It is home to ninety-four different species of butterflies, including the rare Diana fritillary.

mountains.name: Mount Sunflower
mountains.inspirational_story: Set in an endless prairie panorama, this gentle rise offers a quiet, meditative space where the wind blows across a landscape of absolute calm.
mountains.fun_fact: The summit features a whimsical sunflower sculpture made entirely of welded railroad spikes.

mountains.name: High Point
mountains.inspirational_story: Donated out of immense generosity by the Kuser family, this pristine landscape was dedicated to provide a place of rest, recreation, and eternal remembrance.
mountains.fun_fact: The park's beautiful landscape was designed by the Olmsted Brothers, sons of the famous Central Park designer.

mountains.name: Mount Greylock
mountains.inspirational_story: After 19th-century clearcutting stripped the peak, persistent conservation efforts allowed the forest to regenerate, wrapping the mountain in vibrant new life.
mountains.fun_fact: The eerie history and mist of the mountain inspired J.K. Rowling to use it as the setting for the Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry.

mountains.name: Mount Mansfield
mountains.inspirational_story: Viewed from the east, the mountain forms the peaceful profile of a sleeping giant resting eternally under the New England sky.
mountains.fun_fact: The Toll Road has been hosting visitors since 1923, offering a scenic zigzag ascent through vibrant seasonal foliage.

mountains.name: Mount Equinox
mountains.inspirational_story: It is a haven of quiet contemplation, hosting the only Carthusian monastery in North America where monks live in profound silence.
mountains.fun_fact: The mountain features a cascading 'geyser-like' natural spring that gushes out of its side.

mountains.name: Whiteface Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Climbers find deep solace in its soaring heights, using the physical challenge to heal emotional wounds and honor the memory of loved ones.
mountains.fun_fact: The Veterans Memorial Highway allows visitors to drive nearly to the summit, providing accessible sweeping views of the Adirondacks.

mountains.name: Mount Constitution
mountains.inspirational_story: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps during the 1930s, the stone observation tower stands as a lasting monument to community labor and shared environmental appreciation.
mountains.fun_fact: The observation tower at the summit is fashioned after medieval watchtowers from the Caucasus Mountains.

mountains.name: Signal Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Standing apart from the towering Tetons, this isolated peak offers a tranquil space to appreciate the gentle winding of the Snake River far below.
mountains.fun_fact: It was formed not by the same tectonic forces as the Tetons, but by volcanic ashfall from an ancient Yellowstone eruption.

mountains.name: Rendezvous Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: For decades, the iconic aerial tram has gently lifted sightseers above the rugged slopes, democratizing the majesty of the high alpine ecosystem.
mountains.fun_fact: In the winter, riders can spot native wildlife like foxes and ptarmigans from the comfort of the aerial tramway.

mountains.name: Lone Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: The Lone Peak Tram revolutionized mountain access, merging bold engineering with a profound respect for the extreme verticality of the northern Rockies.
mountains.fun_fact: The peak is actually a laccolith, a geological formation where rising magma bowed the earth upward but never erupted.

mountains.name: Mount Lemmon
mountains.inspirational_story: Sara Plummer Lemmon, an intrepid self-taught botanist, climbed the peak in 1881 on her honeymoon, finding empowerment and joy in the natural world.
mountains.fun_fact: It is the site of the southernmost ski destination in the continental United States.

mountains.name: Mount Wilson
mountains.inspirational_story: Perched above the bustling city, its incredibly clear air allowed early astronomers to peer deep into the cosmos, expanding our understanding of a vast, peaceful universe.
mountains.fun_fact: It is home to the historic 100-inch Hooker telescope, which Edwin Hubble used to discover that the universe is expanding.

mountains.name: Mount Hamilton
mountains.inspirational_story: Born from the dream of an eccentric philanthropist, the summit became the world's first permanently occupied mountain-top observatory, bringing humanity closer to the stars.
mountains.fun_fact: The asteroid 452 Hamiltonia, discovered in 1899, is named after this very mountain.

mountains.name: Mount Umunhum
mountains.inspirational_story: Revered by the Ohlone people as 'the resting place of the hummingbird,' the mountain's summit was lovingly restored to honor its sacred heritage and natural beauty.
mountains.fun_fact: You can often catch a glimpse of the Pacific Ocean and the distant Sierra Nevada from its restored observation points.

mountains.name: Mount Tamalpais
mountains.inspirational_story: The mountain's gently sloping silhouette gave rise to the enduring theatrical legend of the Sleeping Lady, a testament to the landscape's ability to inspire art and myth.
mountains.fun_fact: For the Lakota Sioux, it was considered the 'Holy Right Eye of the Great Turtle' that formed the North American continent.

mountains.name: Mount Diablo
mountains.inspirational_story: In Indigenous lore, it was the sacred place where Wek-wek the Prairie Falcon-man helped create the first people and provided them with everything they needed to live.
mountains.fun_fact: During winter, the Spanish used its lower slopes for grazing cattle long before the Bay Area was urbanized.

mountains.name: San Jacinto Peak
mountains.inspirational_story: The mountain's towering presence and accessibility via tramway give everyday visitors the chance to experience profound alpine isolation just minutes from the desert heat.
mountains.fun_fact: Near the summit lies a stone hut built in 1935 by the Civilian Conservation Corps under the direction of a Serbo-Croatian stonemason.

mountains.name: Mammoth Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: The sweeping gondola rides offer thousands of sightseers an effortless glide into the serene heights of the Sierra Nevada, bridging human engineering and natural wonder.
mountains.fun_fact: The summit houses a radio repeater that provides incredible coverage for amateur radio operators across the region.

mountains.name: Stone Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: The Summit Skyride provides an inclusive pathway for people of all abilities to peacefully ascend and appreciate the sweeping geology of this massive monadnock.
mountains.fun_fact: The mountain is an isolated dome of quartz monzonite that formed deep underground and was exposed by millions of years of erosion.

mountains.name: Cannon Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: As the site of North America's first passenger aerial tramway, it sparked a new era of mountain recreation that brought the joy of the alpine world to the general public.
mountains.fun_fact: Its rugged summit observation deck allows visitors to look out over the majestic Franconia Notch.

mountains.name: Wildcat Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Its classic gondola installation in the 1950s opened the skies of Pinkham Notch, granting visitors peaceful, soaring views of the nearby Mount Washington.
mountains.fun_fact: The original 1958 gondolas were distinctively small, looking like 'a VW bus smooshed in like an accordion'.

mountains.name: Jay Peak
mountains.inspirational_story: From a wild mountain where adventurous youth once scrambled, it blossomed into a world-class destination connected by a tram that lifts skiers into the clouds.
mountains.fun_fact: It boasts Vermont's only aerial tram that drops visitors off at a completely treeless summit.

mountains.name: Mount Snow
mountains.inspirational_story: Walt Schoenknecht's eccentric vision transformed a snowy peak into a vibrant playground of innovation, ensuring generations could joyfully experience the winter landscape.
mountains.fun_fact: In the 1960s, the resort built a 'Fountain Mountain' each winter by shooting a geyser of water into the freezing air.

mountains.name: Mount Sunapee
mountains.inspirational_story: After World War II delayed initial tramway plans, the community's determination persevered, eventually opening the mountain to decades of peaceful winter recreation.
mountains.fun_fact: The first ski trail on the mountain was hand-cut by a local ski club using logs from the immediate area for their cabin.

mountains.name: Lookout Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Its sweeping vistas have long provided a quiet perspective over the rolling valleys, inspiring generations of travelers and peace-seeking nature lovers.
mountains.fun_fact: You can supposedly see seven different states from specific vantage points on the mountain on a very clear day.

mountains.name: Black Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Despite being surrounded by heavy industry, the peak remains a forested sanctuary of beautiful hardwoods that resembles the high ridges of the distant Smokies.
mountains.fun_fact: The summit features an abandoned metal fire lookout tower and is the highest natural point in the Commonwealth of Kentucky.

mountains.name: Spruce Knob
mountains.inspirational_story: Once scarred by early 20th-century logging and devastating fires, the mountain has recovered into a protected sanctuary where visitors find serenity in the clouds.
mountains.fun_fact: The high winds at the summit cause the Red Spruce trees to grow one-sided, a phenomenon known as 'flagging'.

mountains.name: Pilot Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Known as 'Jomeokee' or Great Guide, its unmistakable profile provided comforting direction and hope to centuries of weary travelers seeking a new home.
mountains.fun_fact: Its pinnacle was formed by the compression of sand from an ancient beach that existed over a billion years ago.

mountains.name: Sandia Crest
mountains.inspirational_story: The graceful ascent of the aerial tramway invites visitors to leave the desert heat behind and embrace the quiet, cool solitude of the high alpine forest.
mountains.fun_fact: The tramway climbs a staggering 3,819 vertical feet from the base to the crest.

mountains.name: Mount Alyeska
mountains.inspirational_story: The aerial tram glides above the stunning Chugach Mountains, offering a tranquil space to observe the majesty of seven hanging glaciers.
mountains.fun_fact: The mountain features America's longest contiguous double black diamond ski run, descending 2,000 vertical feet.

mountains.name: Hidden Peak
mountains.inspirational_story: Surmounting the rugged Little Cottonwood Canyon via the Snowbird Tram provides an exhilarating yet peaceful detachment from the valley floor below.
mountains.fun_fact: The summit houses a vital amateur radio repeater that forms the basis of the Intermountain Intertie communication network.

mountains.name: Paulina Peak
mountains.inspirational_story: Driving up this ancient volcanic rim rewards travelers with an awe-inspiring panorama of the High Desert, offering quiet reflection on the earth's fiery past.
mountains.fun_fact: The staggering view from the top stretches from the Cascade snow peaks all the way to the remote Great Basin.

mountains.name: Hoosier Pass
mountains.inspirational_story: Once a treacherous route carved by determined prospectors, the paved pass now serves as a scenic, peaceful gateway connecting modern explorers to the Continental Divide.
mountains.fun_fact: The pass was named by nostalgically homesick 19th-century miners who originally hailed from Indiana.

mountains.name: Boreas Pass
mountains.inspirational_story: What was once a perilous, blizzard-prone narrow-gauge railroad line has been transformed into one of the most serene and beautiful scenic drives in the Rockies.
mountains.fun_fact: The route follows an old historic railroad grade connecting Como to Breckenridge.

mountains.name: Loveland Pass
mountains.inspirational_story: The rugged, winding road demands respect and resilience from drivers, rewarding them with raw, breathtaking vistas above the tree line.
mountains.fun_fact: Because it bypasses the Eisenhower Tunnel, it is a vital route for freight carriers hauling hazardous materials across the Continental Divide.

mountains.name: Peak 8
mountains.inspirational_story: Accessible via the BreckConnect Gondola, it has grown from a humble 1960s ski hill into a vibrant nexus of alpine joy and community connection.
mountains.fun_fact: The gondola soars over the protected Cucumber Creek wetlands, which provide a critical habitat for beavers and boreal toads.

mountains.name: Peak 10
mountains.inspirational_story: A rugged summit that effortlessly integrates modern ski infrastructure with wild backcountry access, testing the endurance of high-altitude adventurers.
mountains.fun_fact: The mountain maintains deep snowfields so late into the summer that locals occasionally hold ski events on the Fourth of July.

mountains.name: Bald Mountain
mountains.inspirational_story: Reached via a bumpy, rocky historic mining road, its summit rewards intrepid drivers with profound silence and near 360-degree views of the Tenmile Range.
mountains.fun_fact: The lower portion of the trail passes the remains of an old 1900s ore tramway that once carried silver and lead down the mountain.
